items.readable_text:
Content:
If we want to plot the graph of [MATH: y=-x^2,] we reflect the curve [MATH: y=x^2] in the [MATH: x]-axis, as shown below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/8b05781f3ccba9da5c5cd71796bccc66]

Content:
This transformation is called a reflection in the [MATH: x]-axis, and it occurs because the output [MATH: y]-values of the function are made negative.

Content:
As with the curve [MATH: y=x^2], the vertex of [MATH: y=-x^2] is still at [MATH: (0,0).] However, in the curve [MATH: y=-x^2,] the vertex is the maximum point, because the curve does not go above that point.

Content:
If we combine vertical and horizontal translations with reflection, we get a general form

Content:
[MATH: y=-(x-h)^2 +k.]

Content:

- [MATH: k] units up.

items.title: Combining Reflection with Vertical Translation

sections.normalized_html:
Remember that [MATH: y=-x^2+k] is a reflected parabola [MATH: y=-x^2] that is translated [MATH: k] units up.

The given function [MATH: y=-x^2-3] has [MATH: k=-3.] Therefore, it is a reflected parabola [MATH: y=-x^2] that is translated [MATH: 3] units down.

sections.normalized_html:
Remember that [MATH: y=-(x-h)^2] is a reflected parabola [MATH: y=-x^2] that is translated [MATH: h] units right.

The given function [MATH: y=-(x+2)^2] has [MATH: h=-2.] To see this clearly, we can write the curve as follows:

[MATH: y|= − (x + 2)^{2}; y|= − (x − (− 2))^{2}]

Therefore, the given curve is a reflected parabola [MATH: y=-x^2] that is translated [MATH: 2] units left.

sections.normalized_html:
Remember that the graph of [MATH: y=-(x-h)^2+k] is a translation of the reflected parabola [MATH: y=-x^2] by

  • [MATH: h] units right, and

  • [MATH: k] units up.

The vertex of [MATH: y=-(x-h)^2+k] is located at [MATH: (h,k).]

Here, the parabola is translated [MATH: 2] units right, so we have [MATH: h=2.] The parabola is also translated [MATH: 1] unit up, so we have [MATH: k=1.] We can also see that the vertex is at [MATH: (2,1),] so again we must have [MATH: h=2] and [MATH: k=1.]

Therefore, the equation of the graph is:

[MATH: y|= − (x − 2)^{2} + 1]
